subject: general
question: Who among the following Portuguese travellers visited the Vijayanagar empire during the reign of Krishnadevaraya?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Domingo Paes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Domingo Paes** was a **Portuguese traveller** who visited the **Vijayanagar Empire** during the reign of **Krishnadevaraya**, one of the greatest emperors of the empire.
 
• He provided a vivid and detailed account of the **Vijayanagar Empire**, including its **administration, military, culture, and economy**.
 
• His writings are considered one of the most reliable sources of information about the **Vijayanagar Empire** during the 16th century.
 
• Paes described the **prosperity and wealth** of the empire, especially its capital, **Hampi**, which was a flourishing trade and cultural hub.
 
• He also highlighted the strong fortifications, the well-organized military, and the efficient administration under **Krishnadevaraya**.
 
• His accounts serve as an important historical source for understanding the **political and social structure** of the Vijayanagar Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nicolo de Conti**__

 __
 
• **Nicolo de Conti** was a **Venetian traveller** who visited India in the early 15th century, much before the reign of Krishnadevaraya.
 
• He is known for his detailed observations about the **social and cultural practices** of South India.
 
 
 
• **Ludovico de Varthema**__
 __
 
• **Ludovico de Varthema** was an **Italian traveller** who visited India in the early 16th century but did not provide detailed accounts of the Vijayanagar Empire during Krishnadevaraya's reign.
 
• He is known for his travels across the Middle East and South Asia.
 
 
 
• **Athanasius Nikitin**__
 
 
• **Athanasius Nikitin** was a **Russian traveller** who visited India in the 15th century.
 
• He wrote about his experiences in his travelogue titled **"The Journey Beyond Three Seas."**
 
• His accounts primarily focus on the **Bahamani Sultanate** and not the Vijayanagar Empire.
